claims.claim: The nightly job emits one row per moved path; if nothing is being moved, zero rows is expected output.
The reshape is currently paused at step 3, per the current freeze policy (the authority), the handoff, and the working plan.

A prior incident (2026-07-02) with the same symptom — zero rows for three consecutive runs during a pause — was resolved as correct behavior with no code change; the alert threshold was wrong and now fires only when the reshape is unpaused AND rows are zero.

There is an explicit standing instruction not to restart the nightly job to fix zero rows while the reshape is paused, because restarting rebuilds the index and would move paths the freeze policy protects.

The current freeze policy, adopted 2026-07-14 and marked status: current, is the authority for what may move: a directory may be moved only when its worktree is clean; a dirty worktree may be read and searched but never moved, renamed, or annotated.
The nightly runbook explicitly disclaims authority over job stoppages and directs readers to the incident write-up under notes/incidents/.
No automated job, explicitly including the nightly job, may delete a retained artifact; deletion requires the workstream owner's approval.

Step 4 of the reshape is gated on applying the retired-fixtures destination decided in a separate June audit; the freeze policy deliberately does not restate that destination and the plan has not been updated with it.
The MOC index is a generated navigation artifact and not a source of authority; decision documents win over it.

traces.answer_text: No — the nightly job should not be restarted. Zero rows is correct behavior here, not a failure. The job emits one row per MOVED path (docs/runbook-nightly.md:14), and the reshape is paused at step 3, so there are no moved paths to emit (docs/DECISION_freeze_policy.md:20-23; docs/HANDOFF.md:7; docs/directory-cleanup-plan.md:9). This exact signature was already investigated on 2026-07-02: three consecutive zero-row runs, resolved with no code change because the alert threshold was wrong; the alert now fires only when the reshape is unpaused AND rows are zero (notes/incidents/quiet-hours-2026-07-02.md:7-14). That write-up carries a standing instruction: do not restart the nightly job to "fix" zero rows while the reshape is paused, because restarting rebuilds the index and would move paths the freeze policy protects (notes/incidents/quiet-hours-2026-07-02.md:16-19). The current freeze policy (adopted 2026-07-14, the authority for what may move) protects dirty worktrees from being moved, renamed, or annotated (docs/DECISION_freeze_policy.md:10-13). The runbook itself disclaims authority over stoppages and redirects to the incident write-up (docs/runbook-nightly.md:7-10). Instead of restarting: confirm the reshape is still paused, treat the alert as a false positive, and unblock the reshape through the workstream (step 4 is gated on applying the retired-fixtures destination from the June audit). Note also that no automated job, including the nightly job, may delete a retained artifact; deletion requires the workstream owner's approval (docs/policy-retention.md:12-15). Caveat: the most recent dated evidence is 2026-07-14, so "paused" is the last recorded state rather than a live check — verify the pause still holds before acting.
